# NOTES: *Her Benny: A Story of Street Life* (Silas K. Hocking, 1879, Gutenberg #43325)

Single book. Illustrated by H. Tuck. Publisher: Frederick Warne and Co., London. Dedicated "To My Bairns." Preface: author's pastoral work in Liverpool (three years); characters Benny, Nelly, Perks, Joe Wrag, Granny, Eva Lawrence drawn from life; grouping fictitious. Dated October 21st, 1879.

Setting: Liverpool, mid/late 1870s. Key places: St. George's Church (trysting place, 4 o'clock), Lord Street, Castle Street, Town Hall clock, Landing-stage / Woodside ferry, Park Lane, Scotland Road, Bowker's Row, Addler's Hall (court where Dick Bates's home was), Tempest Court (Betty Barker's), Copperas Hill, Old Hall Street, Falkner Square, Edge Hill, St. John's Market, George's Dock, Brownlow Hill Infirmary, New Cemetery (east of town), Wavertree Park, St. George's Hall, Lime Street Station, Custom House, Eastham Woods / Eastham ferry / New Ferry / Raby Mere / Garston / Aigburth, Birkenhead, Chester, Dartmoor (prison), Scout Farm, Scoutleigh (village, night school, Methodist Sunday-school), Brooklands (Mr. Munroe's house), Scoutleigh Road Station, Manchester.

## Characters
- **Benny (Ben) Bates**: boy, ~11 at start, a year older than Nelly; sturdy, quick, says "by golly," "Golly," "by jabbers," "'mazin'"; learns to read via granny's spectacles/Bible; later learns to write (Mr. Morgan's copies). Honest in principle; steals temptation scene (cross-over); prays "Mr. God."
- **Nelly (Nell) Bates**: sister, 9; pale, thoughtful, big round dreamy eyes, flaxen hair; sees "pictures" (hills, trees, streams) in fire; loves Joe's fire; hacking cough; dies in Infirmary (Children's Ward), buried at public expense, New Cemetery. Last words: "Be good, Benny, an' the Lord will provide, an' we'll meet in heaven." Refrain: "Seaward fast the tide is gliding, / Shores in sunlight stretch away."
- **Dick Bates**: father, drunkard, beats Benny with leather strap for a sixpence; Benny refuses to name the coins; Nelly stops him. Drowns in dock (frost-slippery coping) near the boat; last prayer "Saviour of my Mary, save me!" Dream of children floating in dock.
- **Sall (stepmother)**: coarse drunken woman, "wife" of Dick; calls children "brats."
- **Mary**: Dick's first wife, Nelly's real mother; taught Bible, died; promised to meet in heaven.
- **Joe Wrag**: night watchman, hut with fire, silent, honest, Calvinist ("elect", "reprobate"); calls Nelly "purty little hangel"; had son who ran away ~20 years earlier; wife **Mary Wrag** (sour, later changed by Joe's experiment). Vision of multitude and rainbow "Whosoever cometh unto me." Converts after Nelly's words on "whosoever"; hosts Sunday tea for neighbours (e.g., Dick Somerset).
- **Granny / Betty Barker**: ~70, Tempest Court, Copperas Hill area; husband was Joe's old mate; takes children for 1d per night; reads Matthew 2 at Christmas; Benny calls her granny.
- **Perks**: red-haired thief, plague of Benny; cunning; "gem'men of our perfession"; plots pickpocket/burglary of Jerry Starcher (No. 86, shop); later convicted (burglary and manslaughter), 21 years penal servitude (name John Cadger alias Peeler alias Perks); dies within three years.
- **Bill Tucker**: boy who reports Nelly's injury (dog knocked her, head on stone).
- **Eva Lawrence**: daughter of Mr. Lawrence; under ten at first; gave Benny a new shilling on landing-stage ("Love at Home" song); later grown; saves? (Benny saves her life stopping the horse). Benny keeps the shilling as "lucky shilling."
- **Mr. Lawrence**: Liverpool merchant/man of business; Eva's father; employs Benny at 2s/week above plan; accuses him of stealing £5 note; later finds note in Directory; apologises; offers job in Liverpool; partner later.
- **Mr. Morgan**: clerk, teaches Benny to write.
- **Inspector Sharp**: police, prejudiced, "all rogues."
- **Mrs. Lawrence**: Eva's mother. Servant girl (rude).
- **Preacher/chapel**: chapel near Old Hall Street; gentleman in vestibule takes children to pew; superintendent of Sunday-school.
- **Farmer John Fisher & Mrs. Fisher**: Scout Farm, near Scoutleigh; son Rob died; sons Harry and George (college); baby Winnie ("Benny does not 'ove his 'ittle Winnie"). Mr. Fisher's farm hands/"Giles" (boy with cart, turnips); Mr. Jones, night school at Scoutleigh.
- **Mr. Munroe**: wealthy Manchester merchant, Brooklands; sister is Mrs. Munroe? (Mrs. Munroe is Mr. Lawrence's sister); niece Eva; daughter "Dot"/Miss Munroe.
- **Giles**: shock-headed farm boy with cart, gave Benny turnips.
- Old man farmer near village, offers milk.

## Event sequence
1. Christmas-season Liverpool, fog, Nelly waits by St. George's Church; Benny arrives late after carrying gent's portmanteau to Woodside boat; sixpence (half a bob); roast potatoes at Joe's fire; children sleep at Addler's Hall (home, under stairs, rags/shavings).
2. Addler's Hall: stepmother Sall; Dick beats Benny for money; Nelly intervenes ("You shall not beat Benny so"); children steal bread and butter, plan to leave.
3. Next morning leave with stolen potatoes; cook at Joe's fire; sell matches; sleep in boat turned bottom-up under tow at George's Dock. Footsteps: Dick says "O Death! what dost thou mean?"
4. Joe learns truth; sends them to Betty Barker's at Tempest Court for 1d/night.
5. Dick's remorse; drowns in dock night after; children unaware.
6. Christmas: Benny's business; granny reads Matthew 2; Benny's confusion over "Christ," wearing spectacles; Joe's agony over election/hell.
7. Early new year: children visit Addler's Hall; new children there; wander to chapel; Benny sleeps; Nelly converted in spirit; "Whosoever".
8. Winter; Nelly ill; Joe's vision (rainbow, multitude); storm.
9. Feb: Benny steals cross-over from hosier's; Perks; Benny caught by Nelly; prays "Mr. God".
10. Summer: Perks feud; Eastham Woods outing with Joe; Benny in mud; prize sixpence; Sunday-school hymn "Land ahead!"
11. Autumn: Perks says Nelly killed; Bill Tucker; Benny at Infirmary doorstep prays; sees Nelly; she dies.
12. Joe's grief; Nelly dies; buried at public expense, New Cemetery.
13. Winter; Benny's loneliness; gentleman (Mr. Lawrence) rejects him; girl (Eva) gives shilling; Christmas; Eva sings "Love at Home" under window; Mr. Lawrence hires Benny at New Year.
14. Benny learns writing; visits Mrs. Lawrence with note; Eva with rocking-horse; tells story; Joe's "hangel" speech.
15. Twelve months later (June): Benny promoted prospect; £5 note missing; Benny denies; Sharp; cell; Perks; Sabbath.
16. Joe's experiment: Sunday tea; Dick Somerset; prayer.
17. Perks plans burglary; Benny refuses; released; Perks sent to prison 3 months; Benny's letters to Jerry Starcher and granny (18d); Joe searches.
18. Benny wanders; sleeps in Addler's Hall; sleeps at Nelly's grave; walks country; faints near Scout Farm; Mrs. Fisher's son Rob dead.
19. Joe prays; Benny recovers; "border land"; Benny's crisis; Mrs. Fisher.
20. Benny at Scout Farm; Winnie; night school; six years later; conversion.
21. Accident: Munroe's horse runaway; Benny stops it; arm broken; Eva.
22. Benny visits Brooklands; Munroe offers job in Manchester; Eva's story; recognition.
23. Benny declines Manchester; accepts Liverpool job with Lawrence; visits Eva at bridge; Lawrence apologises.
24. Reward: Benny visits Nelly's grave; Tempest Court demolished (granny dead); Joe found; Benny teaches; Perks convicted; Benny partner with Mr. Lawrence, married Eva; children; shilling.

Ending: Benny and Eva married; children including Ben; moral about honest, truthful living.
